name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
subtitle: National mausoleum and museum park dedicated to Dr Kwame Nkrumah on the historic Polo Ground site.

facts.label: Historic ground
facts.value: Former British colonial polo ground where Nkrumah proclaimed independence on 6 March 1957

facts.label: Mausoleum
facts.value: Houses the tombs of Dr Kwame Nkrumah and his wife Fathia Nkrumah amidst marble reflecting pools

parts.text: The national memorial and resting place of Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, leader of the struggle for Ghanaian independence and pioneer of Pan-Africanism. Located in central Accra on the exact site of the former colonial polo ground where Nkrumah famously proclaimed 'Ghana, our beloved country, is free forever!' at midnight on 6 March 1957, the five-acre park features an upturned sword-shaped marble mausoleum, bronze statues, and an updated biographical museum preserving his personal desk, books, and state gifts.

gaps: Full digital archive of Nkrumah's pan-African audio speeches within the museum is in preparation.
